skill.description: Build three-layer design tokens, component specifications, validation workflows, and brand-compliant HTML presentations with searchable slide guidance.

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are syntax collisions involving Markdown, JavaScript templates, dictionary keys, CSS, or deliberate local file tooling. Confirmed risks are third-party asset requests and a Chart.js CDN example that executes remote code without integrity metadata.

remediation.issue: The documented Chart.js example executes a remote CDN script without Subresource Integrity metadata.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle Chart.js locally, or add a pinned integrity hash and crossorigin attribute to the approved CDN reference.

remediation.issue: Generated slides can contact Pexels and Google Fonts when opened.
remediation.suggestion: Offer local asset embedding and document every external origin before users distribute or open generated decks.

content.user_title: Build Consistent Design Systems and Slides
content.value_statement: Inconsistent tokens and components make design handoffs difficult. This skill structures tokens, validates usage, and generates brand-aligned presentation assets.
actual_capabilities: Defines primitive, semantic, and component token layers with documented naming and reference patterns.
Generates CSS variables or Tailwind color configuration from a token file.
Checks source files and HTML assets for hardcoded design values and missing token usage.
Searches slide strategy, layout, copy, and chart datasets with BM25 ranking.
Generates HTML pitch decks from supported slide data and escapes supplied text.
Suggests curated Pexels backgrounds, overlays, typography, color treatments, and slide layouts.
limitations: Several scripts expect design token assets in a specific parent-project directory structure.
The background helper returns curated remote image URLs but does not download image files.
Generated decks support a fixed set of slide types and reference remote Google Fonts.
Pattern validators do not replace visual review, accessibility testing, or browser compatibility testing.

use_cases.title: Create a Product Design Foundation
use_cases.description: Define reusable color, spacing, typography, state, and component tokens for a new interface.

use_cases.title: Implement Token-Based Frontends
use_cases.description: Generate CSS variables, prepare Tailwind mappings, and inspect source files for hardcoded values.

use_cases.title: Produce Brand-Aligned Presentations
use_cases.description: Select slide strategies and generate structured HTML decks using shared design tokens.

prompt_templates.title: Create Starter Tokens
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a three-layer token plan for [product]. Use [brand colors], [typefaces], and an eight-point spacing scale.
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin a small design system from brand inputs.

prompt_templates.title: Specify a Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Define tokens and states for a [component]. Include default, hover, active, focus, disabled, loading, and error behavior.
prompt_templates.scenario: Prepare a component specification for design and engineering.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Token Usage
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [project directory] for hardcoded colors, spacing, and typography. Group findings by file and propose existing token replacements.
prompt_templates.scenario: Assess an implementation before design-system adoption.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Strategic Deck
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a [slide count]-slide [deck type] for [audience]. Map each slide to a layout, emotion, copy formula, chart, and token treatment.
prompt_templates.scenario: Develop an advanced presentation system with contextual decisions.

output_examples.input: Create a token architecture for a healthcare dashboard with accessible blue and teal branding.
output: Primitive palette with accessible blue, teal, neutral, spacing, radius, and typography scales.
Semantic roles for surfaces, text, actions, status, borders, and focus indicators.
Component aliases for buttons, cards, inputs, tables, and alerts.

output_examples.input: Specify a primary button with complete interaction states.
output_examples.output: A state matrix covers background, text, border, shadow, focus ring, loading, and disabled behavior using semantic aliases.

output_examples.input: Plan a nine-slide investor pitch for a workflow product.
output_examples.output: A slide sequence links narrative goals to layouts, copy formulas, emotional beats, chart choices, and token-based visual treatments.

best_practices: Define raw values once, then reference them through semantic and component aliases.
Validate generated assets and source files before handoff or publication.
Review remote dependencies and replace them with approved local assets when offline delivery matters.
anti_patterns: Do not place raw colors or spacing values directly inside component styles.
Do not create component tokens before defining stable semantic roles.
Do not treat automated token checks as complete visual or accessibility validation.

faq.question: What token layers does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses primitive values, semantic purpose aliases, and component-specific aliases.

faq.question: Can it generate CSS variables?
faq.answer: Yes. The included generator reads token data and produces CSS variables or Tailwind color configuration.

faq.question: Can it validate an existing codebase?
faq.answer: Yes. Its validators detect selected hardcoded colors, dimensions, fonts, and missing token references.

faq.question: Does it create presentation slides?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes slide guidance, searchable datasets, and an HTML generator for supported slide types.

faq.question: Does the background tool download images?
faq.answer: No. It returns curated Pexels URLs, search links, and CSS overlay suggestions.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: Core token work is local. Generated presentations may request Pexels images, Google Fonts, or the documented Chart.js CDN asset.
